answer: In the AI agent economy, each identity earns coins linearly for contributions but incurs a daily copper burn proportional to its network links. Creating a new identity costs 1 copper coin, and each shared juniper node costs 2 copper coins. An attacker spawning identities exponentially incurs a linear copper burn per identity due to shared juniper nodes, while a single honest agent pays minimal copper. Prism tracks juniper access to calculate the burn rate accurately, ensuring the fable of exponential growth is costly.
